//: Every command in stage1 was run once, in this project, before being written here.
//verification: The one thing this repository cannot work out for you: what checks this project has, and where the change stops being under your control once it ships. artifact_kind: service | library | cli | chart | migration | model-boundary | plugin.

stage2: test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo 'working tree is not clean: the artifact would not be the revision under test'; exit 1; }
cargo build --release -p llama-helper && mkdir -p frontend/src-tauri/binaries && cp target/release/llama-helper frontend/src-tauri/binaries/llama-helper-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
cd frontend && npx --yes pnpm@11 run build && ./node_modules/.bin/tauri build --bundles appimage --config '{"build":{"beforeBuildCommand":""},"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'

umask 077; S2=$(mktemp -d /tmp/backchannel-stage2.XXXXXX) && mkdir -p "$S2/home" && printf '%s\n' "$S2" > .git/backchannel-stage2-root && git rev-parse HEAD > "$S2/expected-sha" && APP=$(ls -t target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage | head -1) && test -x "$APP" && printf '%s\n' "$APP" > "$S2/app"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && APP=$(cat "$S2/app") && (HOME="$S2/home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$S2/home/.config" XDG_DATA_HOME="$S2/home/.local/share" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$S2/home/.cache" nohup "$APP" > "$S2/stdout.log" 2>&1 & echo $! > "$S2/pid") && sleep 20 && kill -0 "$(cat "$S2/pid")"
S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && orca-ide status --json | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d['ok'] and d['result']['runtime']['state']=='ready', d"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && PID=$(cat "$S2/pid") && orca-ide computer list-apps --json | PID="$PID" python3 -c "import json,sys,os; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert any(a['pid']==int(os.environ['PID']) for a in d['result']['apps']), 'app not visible to computer-use'"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && PID=$(cat "$S2/pid") && T=$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('frontend/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json'))['app']['windows'][0]['title'])") && orca-ide computer list-windows --app pid:$PID --json | T="$T" python3 -c "import json,sys,os; d=json.load(sys.stdin); w=d['result']['windows']; assert len(w)==1 and w[0]['title']==os.environ['T'] and not w[0]['isMinimized'], w"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && PID=$(cat "$S2/pid") && orca-ide computer get-app-state --app pid:$PID --no-screenshot --json > "$S2/state.json" && python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); t=d['result']['snapshot']['treeText']; assert 'heading Welcome to' in t, t[:800]; assert 'push button Get Started' in t, t[:800]; print('first-launch screen present:', d['result']['snapshot']['elementCount'], 'elements')" "$S2/state.json"

S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && kill "$(cat "$S2/pid")"; sleep 2; S2=$(cat .git/backchannel-stage2-root) && case "$S2" in /tmp/backchannel-stage2.*) ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac && test -d "$S2" && rm -rf -- "$S2" && rm -f -- .git/backchannel-stage2-root
scripts/audio-harness.sh up || { echo 'audio harness could not come up: the audio half of this gate cannot run, and a verdict must say so rather than skip it'; exit 1; }

umask 077; A2=$(mktemp -d /tmp/backchannel-stage2-audio.XXXXXX) && APP=$(ls -t target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage | head -1) && scripts/stage2-record-check.sh "$APP" "$A2" 'ask not' 'country'; RC=$?; APID=$(cat "$A2/pid" 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$APID" ] && { kill -TERM -"$APID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$APID" 2>/dev/null; }; sleep 4; [ -n "$APID" ] && kill -KILL -"$APID" 2>/dev/null; case "$A2" in /tmp/backchannel-stage2-audio.*) rm -rf -- "$A2" ;; esac; scripts/audio-harness.sh down; exit $RC
verification.notes: Product: a Tauri 2 desktop app (Linux AppImage/.deb, macOS .dmg, Windows .exe); artifact_kind 'cli' is the closest kind in the schema for a locally installed application. Development and every verification run happen on Linux only (ADR 0005); macOS and Windows are built in CI and are never proven here - a verdict names them as not proven. Stage 1 history: on 2026-09-02 the suites were found unrun and partly broken (a frontend test reading a file deleted in 3a4ac3a, two tests importing bun:test, one Rust test failing on an f32 round trip); issue #1 fixed them, added the `test` and `typecheck` scripts and the `packageManager` pin, and Stage 1 now runs the full suites. `cargo test --workspace` needs the llama-helper sidecar in frontend/src-tauri/binaries (see Stage 2 prerequisites); 6 Rust tests are #[ignore] by design today. frontend/tests/lib/ignored-tests-are-run.test.mjs does not hold that number -- it holds the partition: every ignored test is either selected by a stage1 command here or excused with a reason there, and an excuse cannot outlive its test. The count itself can change without failing anything, which is why it is written as 'today'. Stage 2 prerequisites: the llama-helper sidecar must be built and copied first (`cargo build --release -p llama-helper` then copy target/release/llama-helper to frontend/src-tauri/binaries/llama-helper-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, exactly the CI step); ffmpeg is fetched by build.rs. Release facts that matter for delivery: release.yml builds macOS and Windows only, Linux bundles exist only as CI artifacts; the updater endpoint, Homebrew cask and Scoop bucket still point at bykof/conversationaly (upstream), not at this fork - a rebrand issue, not a Stage 2 step.
verification.//stage2_unreachable: Only if there is genuinely nowhere to deploy. Set it to WHY, and every verdict narrows to Stage 1 and quotes that reason. Leaving it blank is rejected: a narrowed verdict that cannot say why is the gap this key exists to make visible.
verification.//stage2_unreachable_example: no dev cluster; this is an internal script run by hand
verification.//stage2-ui-record: The conjunction #13 had to record as uncrossed: a device picked *through the UI* and then recorded with, in one instance -- the two existing passes cannot be chained because the application is single-instance. scripts/stage2-ui-record-check.sh does both through WebDriver, and its three modes are the whole point: `signal` plays the sample into the picked monitor's sink and requires the words; `silence` plays nothing and requires their absence; `wrong-sink` plays into a *different* sink and requires their absence, which is what separates 'captured the selected device' from 'captured whatever the machine was playing'. Each run also asserts the application log names the device that was clicked, because a transcript cannot say which channel carried the audio (pipeline.rs mixes both before STT) and a silent fallback would otherwise read as success. Verified 2026-09-04: signal transcribed the sample, both controls stayed silent, and all three opened the picked monitor. Unlike stage2-ui-check.sh this needs the seeded model cache (~1.2 GB, recording is gated on it) and takes minutes, so it belongs in the audio pass that is run by hand: `scripts/stage2-ui-record-check.sh <AppImage> signal|silence|wrong-sink [words...]`.
verification.//stage2-ui: The accessibility-tree driver reaches only top-level push buttons: a `page tab` exposes no action to it, keyboard input does not reach the webview, and a coordinate click delivers no pointer event even with real element bounds. So everything behind the settings tabs was undriven until scripts/stage2-ui-check.sh, which speaks WebDriver to tauri-driver and clicks with real pointer events through WebKit. It asserts the Recordings tab opens, the system-audio picker offers more than the default entry, and the picked one round-trips to recording_preferences.json exactly. That those entries are sink monitors is warranted by configure_linux_audio -- only monitors enter as DeviceType::Output -- not by anything this harness observes; asserting the string 'Monitor of' here would be the display-string class #9 and #10 are about -- the observation #13 recorded as never made. About fourteen seconds on a 24 KB profile with no models, so it belongs in the cheap pass rather than the audio one. Two boundary facts for the verdict: under the driver the app runs with navigator.webdriver true and the webview's automation mode on, switched by TAURI_WEBVIEW_AUTOMATION (tauri-runtime-wry-2.11.4/src/lib.rs:4792); tauri-driver also sets TAURI_AUTOMATION, which is the 1.x name and is read nowhere in this tree. That is not 'as a first-time user would', which the boundary note below claims, so a verdict using this pass must say so. And the driver owns the process, so DELETE /session is the teardown rather than the setsid/pidfile route stage2-record-check.sh uses. One cold run in four fails the handshake with a connection reset, so the script retries five times.
verification.//stage2: The boundary is the installed desktop application: the AppImage built from the tree under test, launched natively on Wayland on a clean profile (fresh HOME/XDG dirs) as a first-time user would. Evidence comes through Orca's computer-use CLI (`orca-ide`; the `orca` shim is broken on this machine, and bare `orca` is the GNOME screen reader) reading the app's AT-SPI accessibility tree. The first pass checks the app starts: the process is alive, it is listed as an app, it has one top-level window with the configured title, the first-launch screen exposes a 'Welcome to ...' heading and a 'Get Started' push button, and the stdout log reports setup complete without a panic. The Linux computer-use provider takes no screenshots, so that pass has no pixel evidence -- but scripts/stage2-ui-check.sh does: GET /session/{id}/screenshot through tauri-driver returns a PNG of the running application, so a verdict may show what was on screen when it drives the UI. The second pass checks audio actually flows, which until #8 no verdict could: scripts/audio-harness.sh makes a PipeWire virtual source the default input and loops a speech sample into it, and scripts/stage2-record-check.sh drives a fresh profile through onboarding and a recording and asserts the sample's words come back as a transcript. The observation is the transcript, not the absence of errors: a harness feeding silence passes every liveness check and fails this one, which is why the harness refuses to report success unless it measures signal. Cost: a clean profile downloads about 4.3 GB before it can record (the transcription model gates recording; a summary model starts on the same screen and is not gated), so this pass takes roughly ten minutes plus the download. The audio pass needs a live PipeWire session and therefore does not run in CI. System audio is covered by the harness but is not run on every gate: `scripts/audio-harness.sh up --system-only --system-home <profile>/home` plus `BC_PREFERRED_SYSTEM_DEVICE='backchannel harness system monitor capture (output)' scripts/stage2-record-check.sh ...` was verified end to end on 2026-09-03 -- the application opened the device and transcribed it while the real microphone delivered silence, so the audio can only have arrived through the system channel. It is left out of the default pass because each app run costs about ten minutes plus its downloads, and a gate nobody waits for is a gate nobody runs; run it by hand when a change touches the system-audio path. Both channels at once is covered as of 2026-09-05 by scripts/stage2-two-channel-check.sh (see the note below). What is still not covered: transcription quality, acoustic bleed between the channels (the harness microphone is virtual, so ADR 0004's real case cannot be reproduced here), and macOS and Windows (ADR 0005).
verification.//stage1-ignored: ADR 0016: a READY verdict on an executable change carries its control table -- the mutation and the output showing each condition going red. Nothing parses a verdict, so this is a rule for whoever writes one, stated here because this is the file the gate is configured from. ADR 0016 makes this machine-enforced rather than remembered: frontend/tests/lib/ignored-tests-are-run.test.mjs fails when an #[ignore]d test is neither named in a stage1 command here nor excused with a reason in that file, when an excuse goes stale, and when a file under tests/ would not match the runner's glob. So adding a stage1 line here is part of adding an ignored test, and the check says so when it is forgotten. Two more ignored tests were added with #13 and are selected by name here for the same reason: `--ignored` alone would also pull in tests that need models or a network. system_audio_monitor_round_trip walks enumeration -> the display string the picker stores -> from_name -> get_device_and_config for every sink monitor, and asserts no monitor leaks into the microphone list; it fails on pre-#13 code with 'no system-audio device was enumerated'. stale_preference_from_the_alsa_era asserts a preference written before the host change errors rather than silently opening another device. Adding a test and not selecting it here is the same as not writing it -- that happened once already. cpal_capture_round_trip stays #[ignore]d because it needs a real input device and microphone permission, which GitHub runners do not have — the CI suites must keep passing without it. It runs here instead, where the machine does have one. It is the guard for the class where enumeration and lookup disagree about a device's identity (#9, #10); it was written, ignored, and therefore did not catch #9. Note it asserts a sample count, not signal: on this machine the capture path returns exact zeros, so a full count of silence passes it.
verification.//stage2-two-channel: scripts/stage2-two-channel-check.sh <AppImage> normal|swapped -- #30's oracle, and the first check in this repository to put speech on BOTH channels at once. The microphone is the harness's virtual source and system audio is a real sink monitor picked through the dropdown, and the two carry DIFFERENT recordings: jfk.wav and dots.wav, whose vocabularies are disjoint (verified by transcribing each through the product path, not inferred from the filenames). The oracle is transcripts.json in the meeting folder rather than the screen, because nothing renders the channel yet -- the OTHERS chip is a design question. `swapped` is the run that matters: a constant label, a label following queue order and a label following loudness all pass `normal`, and only a label that follows the channel passes both. Verified 2026-09-05 on d836442: normal gave 18 segments, 9 'you' / 9 'others', nothing crossed; swapped flipped them. Two things it settles that were previously unmeasured: the harness's default-input swap does take under the PulseAudio host (the app logged Using default microphone: 'Backchannel'), and the description PipeWire reports is NOT the one the harness asks for -- read node.description back from pw-dump, never assert the requested string. Needs the seeded model cache and about three minutes per run, and it plays a speech sample into a real sink for that time, so it belongs in the by-hand audio pass.
